item.description: ### Changed - **The Codex and Cursor integration switches are gone.** Both were on by default and both did nothing at all if you didn't have that agent installed, so for almost everyone they were two controls that never needed touching. Perch still sets up and tears down those integrations exactly as before — `./scripts/uninstall.sh` remains the way to detach it completely. - **The "Codex needs you to trust these hooks again" warning stays**, along with its Re-check button, and now appears only when there's actually something to do. It's the one part of that section that asks something of you rather than offering a preference: Codex won't run a hook it hasn't approved, and it tells you nothing when it skips one. - **The Usage section in Settings is gone.** It had no switches left in it, only a paragraph. What it explained — that the usage bars are fetched from Claude, Codex and Cursor using the logins those agents already saved on this Mac, and that an agent you don't use is never contacted — now lives in `SECURITY.md`, under "What Perch sends off this Mac", along with everything else that leaves your machine.
